refuters.argument:
After a clause-by-clause comparison I found no member of the guarded list and no event on which the printed lemma and the Lean theorem differ in hypotheses or conclusion; the Lean statement renders d1_setup.tex 1107-1113 exactly, and where it differs at all it is strictly stronger (wider n-domain).

Hypotheses. (1) "Let t↦P(t), t∈(−ε,ε), be an event with zero set Z": `E : Event n` (statement file 332-339: radius ε>0, `curve : Set.Ioo (-radius) radius → LabelledTuple n`, continuous, `center_polygon`, `generic_punctured : ∀ t, t.val ≠ 0 → Generic (curve t)`, `nongeneric_center`), i.e. a continuous path of polygons (printed "path of polygons" makes P(0) a polygon, so `center_polygon` is printed content) generic off 0 and not at 0; `E.zeroSet` (482-483) is `{m | m.eval E.center = 0 ∧ ∃ t : E.Parameter, t.val ≠ 0 ∧ m.Relevant (E.curve t)}`, literally the printed Z (event excerpt 6-7), and membership is by index since it is a `Set (Member n)`, as d1_setup 42-218 lines 128-133 require. (2) "g ∈ 𝒢": `m : Member n`; the inductive `Member` (Setup.lean 638-643) has exactly the five printed families with the printed index side conditions (G1 every i; G2 i ∉ {e,e+1}; G5 remote e,f with rep e < rep f; G3 pairwise remote with rep e < rep f < rep g; G4 f,g remote to e with rep f < rep g; `rep i = (i-1).val+1 ∈ {1..n}` is the printed integer representative), and `Member.eval` (648-653) is the printed polynomials G1..G5 (I checked `det`, `edge`, `lineForm`, `row`, `det3`, `G4` against d1_setup lines 45-48, 52-54, 99, 113-118, 128-129; all agree). (3) "relevant at P(t) for some t≠0": `hrel : ∃ t : E.Parameter, t.val ≠ 0 ∧ m.Relevant (E.curve t)` — an existential over off-centre parameters, matching "for some", not "for all". `Member.Relevant P m := m.Unconditional ∨ m.Active P` (683) with `Active` false on G1/G2 and, on G5/G3/G4, exactly "e,f cross" / "e,f,g pairwise cross" / "f and g both cross e" via `Crosses P e f := remote e f ∧ G2 P e f * G2 P e (f+1) < 0 ∧ G2 P f e * G2 P f (e+1) < 0` (402-403), the printed strict-product activation (guarded excerpt 17-22). This is equivalent to the printed "unconditional, or conditional and active" (generic excerpt 3-5). (4) "not a member of Z": `hZ : m ∉ E.zeroSet`.

Conclusion. (5) "g(P(0))≠0": `m.eval E.center ≠ 0`, with `center := curve ⟨0,_⟩` (351). (6) "there is ε'∈(0,ε]": `∃ ε' : ℝ, 0 < ε' ∧ ε' ≤ E.radius`. (7) "g is nonzero and of constant sign on the whole of (−ε',ε')": `∀ t : E.Parameter, |t.val| < ε' → m.eval (E.curve t) ≠ 0 ∧ SignType.sign (m.eval (E.curve t)) = SignType.sign (m.eval E.center)`. Since ε' ≤ ε, the set {t ∈ (−ε,ε) : |t| < ε'} is exactly (−ε',ε'), so the neighbourhood is the printed one, not smaller; and since 0 ∈ (−ε',ε'), "constant sign on the interval" is equivalent to "every sign equals the (nonzero) sign at 0". No weakening, no extra hypothesis, no changed quantifier.

Domain. The only deviation: `Event n` assumes `[NeZero n]` but not `3 ≤ n`, whereas the printed def:polygon fixes n ≥ 3. That makes the Lean theorem a superset of the printed one (stronger), not a narrowing or weakening, so it is not a refutation. I also checked that `remote` (SM.Polygon.lean 63-66: ¬(j−i ∈ {−1,0,1})) is "index sets {i,i+1},{j,j+1} disjoint" as printed, and that `Generic P := IsPolygon P ∧ ∀ m, m.Relevant P → m.eval P ≠ 0` (Setup.lean 1051-1052) is the printed def:generic (A). I did not open work/lean/CV/Events.lean or the proof lines 1114-1121.

Relevance (work/lean/CV/Setup.lean 683): `def Member.Relevant (P) (m) : Prop := m.Unconditional ∨ m.Active P`; Active (674-679): g1/g2 ↦ False, g5 e f ↦ Crosses P e f, g3 ↦ Crosses P e f ∧ Crosses P f g ∧ Crosses P e g, g4 ↦ Crosses P e f ∧ Crosses P e g; printed (cv-def-generic excerpt 3-5): "relevant at a polygon P if it is unconditional, or if it is conditional and active at P".

Activation (Setup.lean 402-403): `def Crosses P e f := remote e f ∧ G2 P e f * G2 P e (f + 1) < 0 ∧ G2 P f e * G2 P f (e + 1) < 0`; printed (cv-def-guarded excerpt 17-22): "Two remote edges e,f are defined to cross when G2_{e,f}G2_{e,f+1}<0 and G2_{f,e}G2_{f,e+1}<0".

Guarded list index data (Setup.lean 638-643): g1 (i), g2 (e i) (i ≠ e ∧ i ≠ e+1), g5 (e f) (remote e f ∧ rep e < rep f), g3 (e f g) (remote e f ∧ remote f g ∧ remote e g ∧ rep e < rep f ∧ rep f < rep g), g4 (e f g) (remote e f ∧ remote e g ∧ f ≠ g ∧ rep f < rep g) — matches guarded excerpt lines 12-14, 60-61, 74-78, 87-93; `rep i := (i-1).val + 1` (337) is the printed representative in {1,…,n} (guarded excerpt 95-102).

Polynomials: G1 P i = det (edge P (i-1)) (edge P i); G2 P e i = det (edge P e) (P i - P e); G5 = det (edge P e) (edge P f); G3 = det3 of rows (−d_{e,2}, d_{e,1}, d_{e,2}p_{e,1} − d_{e,1}p_{e,2}); G4 P e f g = det (edge P f) (P f - P e) * det (edge P g) (edge P e) - det (edge P g) (P g - P e) * det (edge P f) (edge P e) (Setup.lean 365-394); SM primitives det u v = u.1*v.2 − u.2*v.1, edge P i = P (i+1) − P i, remote i j = ¬(j−i ∈ {−1,0,1}) (work/lean/SM/Polygon.lean 16, 49, 63-66) — all equal the printed formulas of d1_setup 45-54, 99, 113-118, 128-129.

Neighbourhood check: with ε' ≤ E.radius the Lean domain {t : E.Parameter | |t.val| < ε'} equals (−ε', ε') as a set of reals, so "on the whole of (−ε',ε')" is rendered exactly; 0 ∈ (−ε',ε') so "constant sign" ⇔ "sign at t = sign at centre".

Only deviation (not a weakening): `structure Event (n : ℕ) [NeZero n]` imposes no `3 ≤ n`, while printed def:polygon (cv-def-polygon excerpt line 2) says "Let n≥3"; the Lean theorem therefore covers n = 1, 2 in addition — a wider domain, Lean stronger than source.
